title: Derivative ideal versus cumulative Taylor-rank minors
statement:
Let $L$ have characteristic zero, $A=L[[W,Z]]$, and $K\subset A$ be an ideal [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix a finite orthant diagram $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$ with ordered vertices, zero $W$ components and essential variables $Z$. Put $d_i=|\alpha_i|$ and form the first-vertex quotient supports $\Delta_i$. Group vertices by equal degree; let $s_\ell$ be the last index of block $\ell$ and $Z^\ell$ its accumulated essential variables. Assume $f_i\in K$ have order $d_i$, unique homogeneous division by their initial forms for every degree prefix with these supports, and $K=\{\sum_iq_if_i:\operatorname{supp}q_i\subset\Delta_i\}$. Assume also that for each accumulated block one can choose $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$, $i(j)\le s_\ell$, with $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)}\in(Z^\ell)$ and invertible $Z^\ell$-Jacobian at zero, and that $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\beta}f_i\in(Z^\ell)$ for $i>s_\ell$, $\beta$ in that block's restricted orthant diagram and $|\beta|\le Q$, where $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. For $t\ge0$, form the finite matrix $B_t$ with columns $Y^\eta f_i(X+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$, $|\eta|\le t$, in the monomial basis of $A[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$; $X=(W,Z)$. Write $r_t=\operatorname{rank}_L B_t(0)$ and let $J_t$ be the ideal generated by the $(r_t+1)$-minors of $B_t$. For every $q\ge\max_i d_i-1$,
$$\sum_{t=0}^qJ_t=(\partial^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i).$$
The minors ideals are independent of the finite generators of $K$. In a smooth finite-type chart their construction commutes with Taylor expansion from any regular generators of the defining ideal. The zero set of $\sum_{t=0}^qJ_t$ is, as a germ at the distinguished point, the Hilbert--Samuel equality locus once $q$ is sufficiently large and the Taylor-module dimension functions take finitely many local values. Hilbert--Samuel here means $t\mapsto\dim_L A/(K+(X)^{t+1})$, including the extended Taylor-module interpretation at nonclosed scheme points.
